title: Workflow for Fluorescence-Targeted Lamella Milling From Vitrified Cells
author: Elise G. Perton
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Vitrified cells containing fluorescently tagged biomolecules of interest Note: The figures in this protocol were prepared using HeLa cells expressing microtubule-associated protein 1A/1B light chain 3B (LC3B) tandem tagged with mRFP and GFP [16]. These cells were also used in our previous publications about the coincident system [1,10] and kindly gifted by Fulvio Reggiori from the University of Groningen, Netherlands. Reagents

AutoGrids composed of: a. Cryo-EM grids (Quantifoil R2/2 Au 200 mesh were used to prepare the figures in this protocol, but other grid types can be used as well) b. C-clip (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number:
c. C-clip ring (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number:
Coverslips Schott D263M glass with ITO coating, diameter 3.4 mm, thickness 0.17 mm (22 × 22 × 0.17 mm cover glass with ITO from Optics Balzers, cut by Lasertec)
Criterium 2 mm mechanical pencil to grip cryo grid boxes, referred to as gridbox pen (BIC, catalog number:
Torlon hex key (Delmic B.V., delivered with system)

Falcon tube with rope attached; a small hole is drilled through the 50 mL Falcon tube near the 45-mark to attach a 2 mm rope that facilitates the transfer of the tube from and to liquid nitrogen (Falcon, catalog number:
Torque limiter set to 10.15 cN×m (Bestool Kanon, catalog number: CN15LTDK-H)

steps.title: Cool cryogenic shields
steps.instruction: Fill both the cryogenic chamber shield dewar and the small dewar mounted at the back of the chamber with liquid nitrogen until boil‑off stops, then fully fill and replace the lids once each dewar is thermalized.

substeps.instruction: Fill the cryogenic chamber shield dewar with liquid nitrogen until the boil‑off prevents further filling (≈5 min).
Fill the small dewar at the back of the chamber with liquid nitrogen until the boil‑off prevents further filling (≈5 min).
When each dewar is thermalized, fill it completely and replace its lid.

steps.title: Cool microcooler
steps.instruction: Start CryoVision, set temperature control to 90 K, log temperature, and wait up to 2 h for the microcooler to reach the set point before loading a sample.

substeps.instruction: Open CryoVision and click the power button to connect to the cooler.
In CryoVision, go to Functions → Start logging.
Set temperature control to 90 K and click Start temperature control.
In the Odemis Chamber tab, turn on the Sample heater if it was off.
Wait (up to 2 h) until the cooler reaches 90 K; then a sample may be loaded.

steps.title: Prepare glovebox
steps.instruction: Open the liquid‑nitrogen dewar, turn on internal lighting, fill the thermos flask, and pre‑fill the sample preparation bath, transfer module, and cold table with liquid nitrogen, allowing the cold table to thermalize.

substeps.instruction: Open the liquid‑nitrogen dewar and switch on the glovebox light.
Press the foot pedal to fill the thermos flask inside the glovebox with liquid nitrogen.
Insert hands into the gloves, then fill the sample preparation bath and the transfer module with liquid nitrogen.
Place the cold table inside the preparation bath if not already there, and place the pickup rod inside the transfer module if not already there.
Wait for the cold table to thermalize (visible by a strong decrease in bubbles).
Add liquid nitrogen to the bath and module as needed to compensate for boil‑off.

steps.title: Mount sample in glovebox
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool tools, open the shuttle, assemble the AutoGrid, spacer ring and screw inside the shuttle, and place the assembled shuttle on the cold table; then start the hot‑plate timer.

substeps.instruction: Place fine tweezers, carbon‑tipped tweezers, gridbox pen and hex key on the hot plate, then slot them onto the cold table to precool their tips; position large tweezers in the preparation bath and wait for thermalization (≈10 min).
Open the shuttle cover with the large tweezers.
Remove the screw from the shuttle with the hex key and place it in an empty recess on the cold table.
Remove the spacer ring with fine tweezers and place it in the same recess.
Take the Falcon tube with its gridbox from the storage dewar and place it in the metal tea‑sieve basket inside the bath.
Insert the gridbox into its recess on the cold table using the large tweezers; remove the lid with the gridbox pen.
Pick up an AutoGrid from the gridbox with carbon‑tipped tweezers and place it in an empty recess on the cold table.
Re‑cap the gridbox with the pen and return the Falcon tube to the storage dewar.
Using fine tweezers, place the AutoGrid inside the shuttle, cells facing upward (grey side up) so the flat side of the AutoGrid faces up.
Insert one fine‑tweezer tip into a small hole of the spacer ring and place the spacer ring in the shuttle with its opening toward the FIB access hole.
Place the screw on top of the shuttle with the hex key and tighten by hand; verify the screw head is below the shuttle surface.
Close the shuttle cover.
Place all tools on the hot plate set to 70 °C and start the hot‑plate timer for 4 h.

steps.title: Load cold table into transfer module
steps.instruction: Attach the pre‑cooled pickup rod to the cold table, transfer the table into the transfer module, and seal the module for transport to the ENZEL system.

substeps.instruction: Screw the pre‑cooled pickup rod into the cold table.
Insert the thinner part of the pickup rod into the aluminum guiding block and pull the cold table into the transfer module until it sits in the bottom mount.
Unscrew and remove the pickup rod.
Close the transfer‑module valve, open the side valve briefly to relieve pressure, rotate the module counter‑clockwise (viewed from above) to undock, then replace the lid.
Transport the sealed transfer module to the ENZEL instrument.

steps.title: Load cold table in ENZEL
steps.instruction: Transfer the cold table from the transfer module into the ENZEL load‑lock, evacuate, and bring the load‑lock to high vacuum.

substeps.instruction: In Odemis → Chamber, click Loading to move the sample positioning stage to the loading position; verify the turbo pump is running.
Remove the lid from the transfer module.
Align the module with the load‑lock chamber, rotate clockwise until the spring pin clicks.
Open the side valve to vent liquid‑nitrogen boil‑off, then close it when atmospheric pressure is reached (hissing from pressure‑relief valve).
Close the gate valve between load‑lock and SEM chamber; close the gate valve between load‑lock and turbo pump; partially open the gate valve between load‑lock and transfer module.
Vent the load‑lock with dry nitrogen via the three‑way valve until atmospheric pressure is reached; then close the three‑way valve.
Open the gate valve between load‑lock and transfer module; lower the vertical transfer‑rod tips into liquid nitrogen to pre‑cool them.
Unfasten the transfer‑rod rest hook; when hissing indicates thermalization, engage the two guiding rods and screw the third rod into the cold table.
Lift the cold table fully out of the transfer module into the load‑lock chamber.
Close the gate valve between load‑lock and transfer module.
Screw the transfer‑rod tip into the lower hole of the cold table (do not force; thread is fragile).
Tighten the vertical transfer‑rod locking screw.
Slowly open the three‑way valve toward the roughing pump while monitoring LN₂ evaporation; avoid aggressive pumping.
When all LN₂ has evaporated, fully open the three‑way valve to the roughing pump and evacuate to 0.1 mbar.
Close the three‑way valve, open the gate valve to the turbo pump, and wait ~30 s after pressure rises.
Enable the infrared CCD camera in xT Microscope Control and turn on the Debian camera module.
Open the gate valve between load‑lock and SEM; monitor chamber pressure (must stay ≤3 × 10⁻⁶ mbar).

steps.title: Load shuttle into ENZEL
steps.instruction: Transfer the shuttle from the cold table into the load‑lock holder using the torque‑limited transfer rod.

substeps.instruction: Verify the Loading button in Odemis is green; click it if not.
Attach the torque limiter (set to 10.15 cN·m) to the end of the transfer rod.
Unscrew the transfer‑rod tip from the cold table and screw it into the shuttle.
Retract the transfer rod to pull the shuttle out of the cold table.
Lower the cold table slightly, then insert the transfer rod ~30 cm while keeping it level.
Lift the rod tip to insert further until the shuttle is visible in the infrared CCD view.
Slide the shuttle fully into the holder until no gap remains between copper and white plastic parts.
Unscrew the transfer rod from the shuttle using the torque limiter; the shuttle shield will rotate around the holder.
Rotate the shield, then retract the transfer rod ~30 cm while moving the hand down slightly to lift the front end.
Level the transfer rod and retract until the tip is centered in the load‑lock chamber.
Close the gate valve to the SEM chamber and secure the rest hook.

steps.title: Unload cold table from ENZEL
steps.instruction: Retract the cold table from the load‑lock, vent, and return it to the transfer module.

substeps.instruction: Loosen the vertical transfer‑rod locking screw slightly.
Open the pressure‑relief valve on the side of the transfer module slightly.
Close the gate valve to the turbo pump.
Partially open the gate valve between load‑lock and transfer module.
Vent the load‑lock with dry nitrogen via the three‑way valve.
When atmospheric pressure is reached (audible click), fully open the gate valve to the transfer module and submerge the cold table into liquid nitrogen.
Close the three‑way valve, verify the cold table is seated in the transfer module, and unscrew the third rod from the cold table.
Lift the two guiding rods out of the cold table and remove the rods from the transfer module.
Close the gate valve between load‑lock and transfer module, stop the turbo pump, and open the roughing pump to evacuate the load‑lock chamber.
Lift the spring pin and rotate the transfer module counter‑clockwise to undock it from the load‑lock, then replace its lid and close the side pressure‑relief valve.
Transport the transfer module back to the glovebox.

steps.title: Unload cold table in glovebox
steps.instruction: Return the cold table from the transfer module to the glovebox and store it.

substeps.instruction: Remove the lid of the transfer module.
Align the module with the glovebox bayonet interface and rotate clockwise.
Open the nitrogen valve to flush the module with dry nitrogen.
Open the roughing‑pump valve for 15 s, then close the dry‑nitrogen valve for 10 s, then close the roughing‑pump valve.
Insert hands into the glovebox gloves, open the transfer‑module valve, and insert the transfer rod into the guiding mechanism.
Lower the rod and screw it into the cold table.
Lift the cold table and place it into the liquid‑nitrogen bath.
Unscrew and store the pickup rod in the guiding mechanism.
Remove hands from the glovebox, start the hair‑dryer timer to avoid condensation, turn off the light, and close the liquid‑nitrogen dewar.

steps.title: Initialize software and stage
steps.instruction: Wake up the FIB/SEM, set scan rotation, load the sample positioning stage, and apply the latest custom alignment.

substeps.instruction: In xT Microscope Control, press Wake‑up (System) to power the FIB and SEM.
Set FIB and SEM Scan Rotation to 180° in xT Microscope Control.
In Odemis → Chamber, click 3Beams, confirm the transfer rod is removed, and click Load.
Wait for the sample positioning stage to be referenced, then cancel the move (Odemis bug).
Click 3Beams again and wait for completion.
In Odemis → Alignment, press Move to latest custom alignment.
Switch to the Localization tab.
If fluorescent streams need setup, open Cryo → Set‑up Streams, remove unwanted streams, and keep two streams per wavelength (live + acquisition).

steps.title: Create SEM overview and select candidates
steps.instruction: Acquire low‑magnification SEM images, identify suitable grid squares, and create features for candidate cells.

substeps.instruction: Enable the RLMAcq stream in the Localization tab.
Hover over the RLM stream, hold right‑mouse button and move to focus the grid foil.
Select the Secondary Electrons stream; set Dwell time 10.2 µs, Scale 16 (256 × 256), HFW 2 mm.
In xT Microscope Control, set SEM to 1 kV, 0.10 nA, magnification 100×; acquire a paused SEM image.
Double‑click the grid centre to centre it in the SEM FOV.
Change Secondary Electrons Scale to 2 (2048 × 2048) and acquire another image.
Press F5 for full‑frame view, locate candidate cells near the centre of a grid square (must be within the middle 40 µm).
Create a feature by clicking Create/Move and then clicking the target location on the SEM image.
Save the SEM overview (File → Save Snapshot As) and exit full‑frame mode (F5).

steps.title: Platinum coat grid with GIS
steps.instruction: Deposit a thin Pt layer using the gas‑injection system to protect vitrified cells and reduce curtaining.

substeps.instruction: In Odemis → Chamber, press Coating.
Enable the infrared CCD camera in xT Microscope Control and wait for the stage to reach the coating position.
In Odemis, click Cryo → Move stage…, set dz = 200 µm, then click Z‑ three times (‑600 µm) while watching the infrared camera.
In xT Microscope Control, open Service Tools → Positioning and click Z to FWD.
In xT Microscope Control, go to Patterning Control → Gas Injection and check the Insert box for the platinum precursor.
Confirm GIS needle insertion when prompted.
In Odemis, click Z+ six times (+1 200 µm) while monitoring holder temperature; if temperature rises, lower stage by clicking Z‑ (‑200 µm).
In xT Microscope Control, click the Closed button of the platinum precursor, wait for the valve to open (audible click), and keep it open for 7–10 s, then click Closed again.
Retract the GIS needle (uncheck Insert).
Move the stage down three Z‑ clicks.
When the Coating button turns green, click Done to close the Move sample stage window.
Click 3Beams to return the stage to its previous position and wait for completion.
In Odemis → Alignment, press Move to latest custom alignment, then return to the Localization tab.

steps.title: Align FIB and SEM
steps.instruction: Coarsely align the FIB and SEM beams using a common feature and set imaging parameters.

substeps.instruction: Enable the RLMAcq stream.
In the SEM overview, locate a feature visible in SEM, FIB, and LM; center and focus it using the RLMAcq right‑click.
Set FIB and SEM parameters as in Table 1:
• SEM: 25 kV, 1,536 × 1,024, Dwell 1 µs, HFW 600 µm, WD 4.4646 mm.
• FIB: 30 kV, 80 pA, 1,536 × 1,024, Dwell 0.1 µs, HFW 150 µm, WD 13.0 mm.
Acquire two images (SEM and FIB), focus, and identify corresponding features (Beam Alignment 1, Coarse).
Run an RLM stream in Odemis and adjust focus to determine the Z shift needed to centre the same feature in both FIB and SEM fields.
Optionally increase magnification in both modalities and repeat the coarse alignment for higher precision.

steps.title: Align FIB and LM
steps.instruction: Fine‑align the FIB with the reflective‑light microscope using terminal commands and a cleaning cross‑section pattern.

substeps.instruction: Open a terminal.
Run `odemis-cli --move align z 5` (adjust µm value and sign as needed) to move the objective lens in Z until the RLM is in focus.
Center the RLM on the previously aligned feature with `odemis-cli --move align x 5` and `odemis-cli --move align y 5` (adjust as needed).
Move to a flat region on the grid and focus the RLM by moving the stage (do not use the terminal for stage moves).
Set FIB current to 2.5 nA in xT Microscope Control and focus.
Mill a 2 µm × 2 µm cleaning cross‑section centred in X with the pattern top at the centre of the Y FOV (Beam Alignment 1, Fine).
Use the terminal commands again to shift the objective lens so that the alignment pattern is centred in X and the Y centre aligns with the foil edge.
Repeat the move‑to‑flat‑region, focus, and cross‑section steps at a second location; stop when alignment is satisfactory.

steps.title: Check and refine targets
steps.instruction: Update Z positions, discard broken or ice‑contaminated features, and associate fluorescence with SEM features.

substeps.instruction: Enable RLMAcq in the Localization tab.
For each SEM feature:
i. Click Create/Move, drag the feature to the centre of its grid square.
ii. Bring the foil into focus and click Use current Z to store Z.
iii. If crystalline ice on the backside or a broken foil is observed, set Status to Discarded.
Switch to a fluorescence stream.
For each feature with Status = Active:
i. Click Create/Move, drag the feature onto the corresponding fluorescent spot.
ii. Bring the fluorescent spot into focus and click Use current Z.
iii. If no suitable fluorescence is present, set Status to Discarded.

steps.title: Automated rough milling
steps.instruction: Run the iFast script to perform relief cuts and rough milling on all Active features, then clean lamellae at 30 kV, 2.5 nA.

substeps.instruction: Open the iFast developer, click Open, navigate to the iFast script “lamella milling”, and click the Run icon.
In Odemis, select Milling → Auto mill → Relief cuts & rough milling → Run action.
Wait for rough milling to finish (≈6 min per feature; total ≈1 h depending on number of targets).
Inspect all Active features with fluorescence microscopy; discard any that lost signal or have broken lamellae.
In xT Microscope Control, clean each Active lamella using the FIB at 30 kV, 2.5 nA.

steps.title: Automated lamella thinning to ~2 µm
steps.instruction: Decrease FIB current to 0.79 nA, re‑align FIB‑LM, and run the 2 µm thinning script on Active features.

substeps.instruction: Set FIB current to 0.79 nA and bring into focus.
Repeat the FIB‑LM alignment described in step “Align FIB and LM” (using 0.79 nA).
For each Active feature, bring the fluorescent target into focus, update Z, and ensure Status remains Active.
In Odemis, select Milling → Auto mill → 2 µm milling → Run action.
Wait for thinning to complete (≈6 min per feature; ≈1 h total).
Check all Active features with RLM; discard any broken lamella.
Check all Active features with fluorescence; discard any that lost signal.

steps.title: Manual lamella thinning
steps.instruction: Thin each lamella by hand while monitoring fluorescence intensity with the IFM‑Monitor notebook.

substeps.instruction: Center a fluorescent feature inside the lamella in the FM stream and keep the stream running.
Set FIB current to 0.23 nA and focus.
Open a terminal, run `jupyter-notebook`, navigate to IFM‑Monitor.ipynb, open it, and run the notebook to display live maximum (orange) and mean (blue) pixel intensity around the FM crosshair.
Draw a cleaning cross‑section and begin thinning; stop immediately if fluorescence intensity drops sharply, then resume from the opposite side.
Pause the FIB before switching light‑imaging channels or before stage movements; acquire a new FIB overview after each pause.
Measure lamella thickness using the interference‑pattern width w in RLM and compute d = 0.174 w (use the ruler icon).
Note that the Pt layer appears as a bright white band in RLM; if it disappears, stop milling.

steps.title: Polish lamella
steps.instruction: Evenly polish the lamella surface using a low‑current FIB beam.

substeps.instruction: Decrease FIB current to 80 pA.
Mill the lamellae to obtain an even surface; aim for uniform RLM intensity, which indicates consistent thickness.

steps.title: Acquire final overview images
steps.instruction: Capture a final SEM overview of the grid before unloading.

substeps.instruction: In Odemis, go to Milling → Auto mill → Relief cuts & rough milling → Acq images.
Center on the grid and acquire a SEM overview image.
Save the image (File → Save Snapshot As).

steps.title: Prepare ENZEL for sample unloading
steps.instruction: Start the turbo pump, verify low pressure, and move the sample positioning stage to the loading position.

substeps.instruction: Start the turbo molecular pump.
Confirm the load‑lock chamber is being pumped by the roughing pump and pressure is <0.1 mbar.
When turbo pump speed exceeds 50 %, close the three‑way valve and open the gate valve between turbo pump and load‑lock.
In Odemis → Chamber, click Loading to move the stage to the loading position.

steps.title: Unload shuttle in ENZEL
steps.instruction: Detach the shuttle from the transfer rod and place it back into the cold table.

substeps.instruction: Attach the torque limiter to the transfer‑rod tip.
Unscrew the transfer‑rod tip from the cold table.
Lower the cold table slightly.
Insert the transfer rod 30 cm while keeping it level.
Lift the rod tip to engage the shuttle and rotate the torque limiter until it clicks (full engagement).
Retract the transfer rod 30 cm while moving the hand down slightly to lift the front end.
Level the rod and retract until the shuttle sits inside the load‑lock chamber.
Close the gate valve to the SEM chamber and secure the rest hook.
Lift the cold table and insert the shuttle into the cold table.
Unscrew the transfer rod from the shuttle.

steps.title: Warm microcooler and end‑of‑day checks
steps.instruction: Stop cooling, check gas bottle level, shut down the instrument, and leave the system ready for the next day.

substeps.instruction: In CryoVision, click Stop temperature control; confirm the stop.
Check the liquid‑nitrogen bottle level in CryoVision; replace if below 15 %.
In xT Microscope Control, press Sleep (System) to shut down the FIB‑SEM.
Close the three‑way valve and open the gate valve so the load‑lock chamber is pumped by the turbo pump.
If no further work is planned, top up the small dewar at the back of the chamber with liquid nitrogen.

description: Validation of protocol TEM images of the lamellae depicted in Figures 3 and 4 are included in Figure S3. We acquired a tomogram of an autolysosome (Figure S4 and Video S1). All TEM images were acquired on a JEOL JEM3200-FSC operated at 300 kV. For the montage in Figure S3A and B, 6 × 6 images at 2,500× magnification (1.152 nm per pixel) were stitched together using PySerialEM [19]. For the tomogram in Figure S4 and Video S1, MotionCor2 was used to motion-correct the movies [20]. Tilt-series alignment and tomogram reconstruction were performed with the IMOD tomographic package [21]. Tomograms were reconstructed with WBP and with a 10-iteration of the SIRT-like filter. The tomogram was denoised using TOPAZ-Denoise. The movie was made with ChimeraX [22]. Using the ENZEL system, Wang et al. [15] were able to investigate the NLRP3 inflammasome in situ. This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research articles: • Figure 6 in Boltje et al. [1]. A cryogenic, coincident fluorescence, electron, and ion beam microscope. eLife , 11, e82891. https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.82891 • Figure 7 in Boltje et al. [10]. Thickness- and quality-controlled fabrication of fluorescence-targeted frozen-hydrated lamellae. Cell Reports Methods , 5(3), 101004. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crmeth.2025.101004
